headline: Hockey Canada hires Dustin Schwartz as head of goaltending
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Hockey Canada has hired Dustin Schwartz as its head of goaltending. Schwartz was most recently the goaltending coach of the Edmonton Oilers, per the outlet's summary.

The move matters for Edmonton because the Oilers have been winning, but not mostly because of their goaltending. EDM is 11-2-2 and has controlled 53% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality, not just shot volume) so far this season. Yet the team's goalies have saved 2.6 fewer goals than expected given the shots they faced, so the results have come from elsewhere. EDM has scored 17 more goals than its chances would predict, which suggests finishing is carrying the record. At five-on-five the Oilers hold only 49% of the expected goals, so the edge comes from the power play (0.91 expected goals per game), not even-strength play. It's a small sample, but if the goaltending doesn't improve, the cushion may be thinner than 24 points in 15 games suggests.
